root_cause: CHG-2318 lowered the PgBouncer default_pool_size for payments-db from 60 to 25 server connections, below what payments-api needs at evening peak, so requests waited at PgBouncer and timed out after 5 s.
key_facts: PgBouncer default_pool_size was reduced from 60 to 25 by CHG-2318 on 2026-11-03.
sv_active is pinned at 25 with clients waiting, so the server pool is the bottleneck.
Same mechanism as PM-2025-007 (client demand above the PgBouncer pool).
expected_fix: Restore default_pool_size to 60 (or move the reconciliation job to a separate pool) and recheck the capacity rule.

root_cause: checkout-api v5.8.0 (CHG-2331) writes carts with plain SET and no TTL; with maxmemory-policy volatile-lru only keys that have a TTL can be evicted, so cart-cache filled to maxmemory and Redis rejected writes with OOM errors.
key_facts: CHG-2331 moved carts to CartStore, written with plain SET; the cleaner job is disabled.
volatile-lru evicts only keys with an expiry (CHG-2201, PM-2026-002); evicted_keys=0 and almost no keys have expires.
Redis returns "OOM command not allowed" when it cannot evict at maxmemory.
expected_fix: Roll back to v5.7.2 or set TTLs on cart keys; then expire or delete the TTL-less keys.

root_cause: inventory-api v3.12 (CHG-2325) added one catalog-api call of about 0.8 s per reservation message; with max.poll.records=500 a batch takes about 400 s, longer than max.poll.interval.ms of 300 s, so the consumer is evicted from the group and rebalances in a loop.
key_facts: CHG-2325 added a per-message catalog-api call of 700-900 ms.
500 records x ~0.8 s is about 400 s, above max.poll.interval.ms 300000.
Same mechanism as PM-2025-019; its action item to reduce max.poll.records (FUL-312) is still open.
expected_fix: Roll back the enrichment or lower max.poll.records (e.g. 50) and batch/cache the catalog lookups.

root_cause: Raising search-querylog-* retention from 7 to 90 days (CHG-2309) let query log indices accumulate until data nodes crossed the 95% flood-stage watermark; OpenSearch put a read-only-allow-delete block on the indices, so the indexer's writes were rejected.
key_facts: CHG-2309 increased query log retention to 90 days at about 18 GB per day.
Flood stage (95%) applies index.blocks.read_only_allow_delete.
Related disk-watermark history in PM-2025-011.
expected_fix: Delete or shrink old query log indices, revert retention, then remove the read-only block once disk is below the watermark.

root_cause: CHG-2340 cut the order-worker memory limit from 1Gi back to 512Mi based on average usage, but peak usage is about 700 MB, so pods are OOMKilled (exit 137) and crash loop.
key_facts: CHG-2340 set memory limit 512Mi (was 1Gi) from October averages.
Peak RSS is about 700 MB (PM-2026-005); the handbook says size from peak plus headroom.
expected_fix: Restore the 1Gi limit and size limits from p99 peak plus 30%.

root_cause: Paygate switched its server chain to the 'Paygate Issuing CA G3' intermediate on 2026-11-14 09:00 UTC (CHG-2302), but the payments-api trust bundle ConfigMap was never updated (PAY-881 not applied), so payments-api no longer trusts Paygate's certificate.
key_facts: CHG-2302 announced the G3 intermediate from 2026-11-14 09:00 UTC; status scheduled, not applied.
payments-api verifies Paygate against the hand-maintained ConfigMap paygate-ca-bundle.
The error is about the server chain (unknown authority), not the client certificate (renewed by cert-manager).
expected_fix: Add Paygate Issuing CA G3 to paygate-ca-bundle and restart or reload payments-api.

root_cause: CHG-2336 fixed CoreDNS at 2 replicas and disabled the proportional autoscaler; at sale-evening load the two pods saturated their CPU, and lookups across all services timed out.
key_facts: Errors in unrelated services at once point to shared infrastructure; all are DNS lookup failures.
CHG-2336 reduced CoreDNS to 2 replicas and disabled the autoscaler (min was 6).
Same mechanism as PM-2025-022; ndots:5 amplifies query volume.
expected_fix: Re-enable the proportional autoscaler (min 6) and scale CoreDNS now.

root_cause: Flyway V87 (CHG-2321) dropped idx_variant_sku and replaced it with a composite index on (product_id, sku); queries filtering on sku alone cannot use it, so the hot SKU lookup sequentially scans 42M rows.
key_facts: CHG-2321 dropped idx_variant_sku; the new composite index leads with product_id.
Lookups by sku are the hottest query; the plan shows a Seq Scan.
PM-2025-024 required EXPLAIN plans for hot queries in migration review.
expected_fix: Create an index on sku CONCURRENTLY (or restore idx_variant_sku).

root_cause: notification-service v2.4 (CHG-2328) replaced the backoff-and-Retry-After sender with the shared http-client's immediate retries; once the campaign hit the shared PostRelay limit, immediate retries burned the remaining quota and kept the account throttled.
key_facts: CHG-2328 uses up to 5 immediate retries on any non-2xx, ignoring Retry-After.
CHG-2215 had added backoff with jitter and Retry-After after PM-2026-004; v2.4 undid it.
The campaign shares the 100 messages/s PostRelay limit.
expected_fix: Configure the http-client to back off with jitter and honour Retry-After (or roll back to v2.3); pause the campaign to drain.

root_cause: inventory-api v3.13 (CHG-2333) removed the deprecated available_qty field from /v2/availability while checkout-api still requires it, so checkout-api fails to deserialize the 200 responses. The share of failures follows the inventory-api rollout.
key_facts: checkout-api has no deploy; the failing call is to inventory-api, which returns 200.
CHG-2333 removed available_qty in favour of quantity_available.
checkout-api maps the response to a strict DTO (service notes).
expected_fix: Roll back inventory-api v3.13 (or restore the field), then move checkout-api to quantity_available.
